canonical_name: AI2D (AI2 Diagrams): 'A Diagram Is Worth A Dozen Images', Kembhavi et al. (AI2), ECCV 2016 - diagram question answering
metric: accuracy (%) on 4-option multiple-choice diagram questions, test split; two image variants in use: 'without mask' (original labels, used by OpenAI/Anthropic/Google) and 'with mask' (VLMEvalKit AI2D_TEST, used by OpenCompass/Qwen/InternVL)
ab_source: https://openai.com/index/hello-gpt-4o/ (2024-05-13; scores shown in chart image); number confirmed in Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet model card addendum Table 2 'AI2D (test) ... GPT-4o 94.2%' https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/fed9cc193a14b84131812372d8d5857f8f304c52/Model_Card_Claude_3_Addendum.pdf and InternVL2.5 report Table 7 'AI2D (w/wo M)' GPT-4o-20240513 84.6/94.2 https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.05271
strict_system: Gemini 2.5 Pro (thinking), evaluated independently by the Qwen team (AI2D with mask)
strict_score: ~90 (90.0 or 90.9; extraction from PDF table ambiguous)
strict_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.21631 (Qwen3-VL Technical Report v1 2025-11-26, Table 2 row 'AI2D w. M.'; caption note: only '*' values are sourced from tech reports, Gemini value unstarred)
n_items: ~3,088 test questions (test split = 1,000 of 4,903 diagrams; lmms-lab/ai2d test split 3.09k rows); full dataset ~15K questions
lineage: Parent of TQA (Textbook QA, AI2, 2017) and AI2D-RST (2020) diagram resources; no official successor version. Same organization (AI2) later used it as a headline eval for Molmo (2024-09).
best_by_cutoff: 96.3 - Molmo-72B (AI2, no-mask/opaque+transparent boxes, arXiv 2409.17146, 2024-09-25); with-mask variant: Qwen3.6-Plus 94.4 (2026-04-01, qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen3.6), Gemini 3 Pro 94.1 as run by Qwen (Qwen3.5 card, 2026-02-16)
notes: No human baseline in the paper (checked PDF) -> criterion B (90). Before 2024-05 the best results were Claude 3 Sonnet/Opus 88.7/88.1 (2024-03-04), Grok-1.5V 88.3 (2024-04-12), Gemini 1.5 Pro (Feb) 80.3; prior fine-tuned SOTA PaLI-X 81.4. GPT-4o 94.2 (2024-05-13) is first >=90; Gemini 1.5 Pro (May 2024) 94.4 and Claude 3.5 Sonnet 94.7 (2024-06-20) follow. Variant issue: OpenCompass/VLMEvalKit independent 'with mask' runs give GPT-4o 84.6, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 81.2, Gemini 1.5 Pro 79.1 (InternVL2.5 Table 7) - a different, harder image variant, so not treated as refutation of the >=90 no-mask self-reports (judgement call). With-mask variant first >=90 only ~2025-11 (Gemini 2.5 Pro in Qwen runs) / 2026-01 (Kimi K2.5 90.8 self). Strict: no organizer leaderboard exists; earliest independent single-model >=90 found is the Qwen3-VL report's run of Gemini 2.5 Pro (same tables were released as images with Qwen3-VL on 2025-09-23, image host unreachable); firmer later evidence: Qwen3.5 card (2026-02-16) independent runs GPT-5.2 92.2, Gemini 3 Pro 94.1. Still reported by Qwen in 2026. Sources unreachable: OpenCompass leaderboard JSON (expired cert), Qwen table images (aliyuncs blocked).

canonical_name: ActivityNet-QA: A Dataset for Understanding Complex Web Videos via Question Answering (Yu et al., AAAI 2019)
release_source: https://github.com/MILVLG/activitynet-qa (commit 89cdb05 'add dataset' 2019-01-24, before AAAI-19; arXiv version https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.02467 only 2019-06)
metric: accuracy (%) on open-ended QA, test split (original: exact match; LMM era usually GPT/LLM-judged accuracy following Video-ChatGPT)
abandoned_evidence: Last report by any of the 9 labs: Gemini 2.5 technical report (2025-06-17, ActivityNet-QA visual-only 66.7). No later lab reports found (Qwen3-Omni 2025-09 and Qwen3-VL 2025-11 reports do not include it; not in Gemini 3 / Kimi / Muse materials per input data) -> >15 months without lab reports by 2026-09-30. No official leaderboard (GitHub repo only ships an eval script; last commit 2020-01); Papers-with-Code leaderboards closed 2025-07.
score_at_release_system: E-SA (creators' baseline; overall accuracy on test, AAAI 2019 paper)
n_items: 8,000 QA pairs on 800 test videos (train 32,000 / val 18,000 / test 8,000; 58,000 total)
lineage: Built on ActivityNet v1.3 videos (2015); sibling VideoQA sets MSVD-QA/MSRVTT-QA/TGIF-QA; LMM-era GPT-assisted scoring protocol from Video-ChatGPT (2023-06). No official successor.
best_by_cutoff: ~67: PLM-8B 67.3 (Meta PerceptionLM, LLM-judge accuracy, arXiv 2504.13180, 2025-04); Gemini 2.5 Pro 66.7 (visual-only, Gemini 2.5 tech report 2025-06-17)
notes: Paper reports no human performance (checked PDF) -> criterion B. Lab trajectory: Gemini Ultra 52.2 (2023-12), Gemini 1.5 Pro 56.7 (2024-02), GPT-4o 61.9 (2024-05 chart), Llama 3-V 70B 56.3 (2024-07), Gemini 2.5 Pro 66.7 (2025-06) - far from 90. Scoring protocol drift (exact match vs LLM judge) makes cross-paper numbers only roughly comparable. Abandonment judged on lab reports + absence of any official leaderboard; academic video-LLM papers may still cite it (not leaderboard activity). Test answers public since 2019-05 (commit 'add test_a.json').

canonical_name: BLINK: Multimodal Large Language Models Can See but Not Perceive (Fu et al., ECCV 2024)
metric: accuracy (%) on multiple-choice questions, averaged over 14 perception tasks (overall)
score_at_release_system: GPT-4V (test; 51.14 on val) - best model in paper
n_items: 3,807 MCQs: val 1,901 (public answers) / test 1,907 (answers hidden, EvalAI)
lineage: Reformats 14 classic CV tasks (depth, correspondence, forensics, IQ tests, etc.) into MCQs; no official successor version found. Same group later released related multi-image benchmark MuirBench (2024-06, listed on project page).
best_by_cutoff: 78.9 - Kimi K2.5 (thinking), Moonshot tech report arXiv 2602.02276 (2026-01/02); Gemini 3 Pro 78.7 in Moonshot internal eval
notes: Human baseline reported per split in Table 1 (val 95.67 / test 95.70; per-task 80-100, IQ-test human score 'annotated by authors'); protocol is in Appendix A.4, which I could not read (arXiv HTML/PDF truncated by fetch tool) - treated as average human -> criterion A (also >=85). Under criterion B (90) the status would be the same: best ~79. Test labels hidden (EvalAI since 2024-04-24); community reports val (split=dev). Official val leaderboard (static/val_result.csv in github.com/zeyofu/blink) last updated 2024-07-11 (GPT-4o 60.04 top). Lab reports: Gemini 1.5 Pro (2024-05), Qwen3-VL report 2025-11 (BLINK 70.7; Gemini 2.5 Pro 70.6 from its report), Kimi K2.5 2026-01 (78.9) -> not abandoned.

canonical_name: BabyVision: Visual Reasoning Beyond Language (Chen et al., UniPat AI, 2026)
metric: accuracy (%) - Avg@3 of pass@1, answers checked for semantic equivalence by an LLM judge (Qwen3-Max / GPT-5.2) against ground truth
lineage: Companion tracks BabyVision-Gen (image-generation evaluation) and BabyVision-Mini (20-item developmental comparison) released together (2026-01); cites BLINK (2024-04) as closest predecessor on perception. No successor by cutoff.
best_by_cutoff: No tools: 82.0 - Qwen3.8-Max (official leaderboard unipat.ai/benchmarks/BabyVision, 2026-08-03; Qwen blog qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen3.8). With tools (non-standard): 91.3 Qwen3.8-Max with code interpreter (2026-08-03); DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash w/ tools 89.6 (HF card 2026-09-10).
notes: Human baseline: 16 adults with >= bachelor's degree completed all 388 questions; abstract: 'the average adult score of 94.1' -> criterion A (>=85%). Children baselines (ages 3-12) only on the 20-item BabyVision-Mini. Standard protocol: unified prompt, highest reasoning effort, no tools; lab results 'w/ python'/'with CI'/'with tools' are tool-assisted (Qwen3.5 card: 52.3 with CI vs 43.3 without). Official leaderboard (last updated 2026-08-03, 29 entries) ranks tool and no-tool runs together; top: Qwen3.8-Max with tools 91.3, Claude Fable 5 with tools 90.5, GPT-5.6 Sol with tools 88.9 - all below 94.1, so no event even if tools were allowed. Very rapid climb: 49.7 (2026-01) -> 82.0 no-tools (2026-08).

canonical_name: CharXiv: Charting Gaps in Realistic Chart Understanding in Multimodal LLMs (Wang et al., Princeton, NeurIPS 2024 D&B) - unit coded on its primary metric, Reasoning-question accuracy (CharXiv-R / RQ)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.18521 (v1 2024-06-26); leaderboard site github.com/charxiv/charxiv.github.io first results commits 2024-06-24/25; data in github.com/princeton-nlp/CharXiv (initial commit 2024-06-12)
metric: accuracy (%) on reasoning questions (1 per chart), graded by GPT-4o against reference answers; leaderboard ranked by Reasoning Overall (Descriptive accuracy is the secondary column)
score_at_release_system: Claude 3.5 Sonnet (official val leaderboard at launch, commit 2024-06-25; paper v1 text cites GPT-4o 47.1 as strongest)
n_items: Reasoning: 1,000 val + 1,323 test questions (one per chart); Descriptive: 4,000 val + 5,292 test; 2,323 charts total
lineage: Successor-in-spirit to template-based chart QA (ChartQA 2022-03, PlotQA, DVQA); OpenAI also derived 'CharXiv Missing Image' deception eval (GPT-5.x system cards). No official CharXiv v2 by cutoff (repo still 'v1.0').
best_by_cutoff: No tools: 88.9 - Claude Mythos 5 (system card 2026-06-09, per input lab report; PDF too long to verify); others 88.4 Qwen3.8-Max without CI (2026-08-03), 88.4 Muse Spark 1.1 (2026-07-09), 86.2 Gemini 3.8 Flash (model card 2026-09). With Python tools (non-standard): 93.5 Claude Mythos 5 / Qwen3.8-Max with CI.
notes: Primary metric = Reasoning (abstract headline 'GPT-4o 47.1% ... human 80.5%'; leaderboard sorted by Reasoning). Human = graduate students with ML background (data/sources/Human.txt), measured on the validation set used by the leaderboard -> 80.5 < 85 -> criterion B (90). Test answers withheld ('we do not release answers for test'); official leaderboard and all lab reports use val (split=dev). Official leaderboard last updated 2025-04-21 (o3 high 78.6 top). Standard protocol has no tools; no no-tool result >= 90 found by 2026-09-30 (GPT-5.2 82.1 no tools / 88.7 with Python, 2025-12-11; GPT-5.4/5.5 pages do not report CharXiv; Gemini 3.7 Flash 84.5 no tools / 88.7 with tools; Gemini 3.8 Flash card lists GPT-5.6 Sol ~85.8 no tools). Tool-assisted >= 90 (not counted): Claude Mythos Preview 93.2 with Python (2026-04-07), Opus 4.7 91.0 (2026-04-16), Kimi K3 91.3 (2026-07-16), Qwen3.8-Max 93.5 with CI (2026-08-03). Models exceed the human reasoning baseline since ~2025-04 (o3 78.6 near; Gemini 3 Pro 81.4 in 2025-11). Sensitivity on Descriptive (human 92.1, criterion A): o3 (high) 95.0 and o4-mini 94.3 on the official leaderboard (commit 2025-04-21) would mark 2025-04. Claude 'with image-cropping tool' numbers (Opus/Sonnet 4.6) are tool-assisted.

canonical_name: ChartQA: A Benchmark for Question Answering about Charts with Visual and Logical Reasoning (Masry et al., Findings of ACL 2022)
metric: relaxed accuracy (%) on test (numeric answers within 5% of gold, exact match otherwise); overall = average of ChartQA-H (human) and ChartQA-M (augmented) test sets
c_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05506 (ChartQAPro, v1 2025-04-07; authors incl. Ahmed Masry, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque - 3 of 5 ChartQA authors)
c_quote: existing benchmarks like ChartQA lack real-world diversity and have recently shown performance saturation with modern large vision-language models (LVLMs). To address these limitations, we introduce ChartQAPro
score_at_release_system: VisionTaPas with extracted data tables (creators' best, test overall; 59.3 with gold tables)
n_items: 2,500 test questions (ChartQA-H 1,250 on 625 charts + ChartQA-M 1,250 on 987 charts)
lineage: Predecessors: FigureQA, DVQA, PlotQA (templated chart QA). Successor by same group: ChartQAPro (2025-04-07, explicitly motivated by ChartQA saturation). Google switched to an internal 'BetterChartQA' in the Gemini 2.5 report (2025-06-17, no description given). CharXiv (2024-06) also positioned against ChartQA-style templated benchmarks.
best_by_cutoff: 90.8 - Claude 3.5 Sonnet (2024-06-20; same score for Claude 3.5 Sonnet new, 2024-10-22); later >=90: Llama 4 Maverick 90.0 (2025-04-05 model card), Qwen3-VL-235B 90.3 (arXiv 2511.21631)
notes: No human accuracy in the paper (only crowd agreement 61.04% exact / 78.55% lenient) -> criterion B. Trajectory before the event: Gemini Ultra 80.8 (2023-12), Claude 3 Opus 80.8 (2024-03), GPT-4o 85.7 (2024-05-13), Gemini 1.5 Pro May-2024 87.2; specialised chart models (TinyChart, ChartGemma, ChartMoE) stayed in the 80s -> first >=90 is Claude 3.5 Sonnet 90.8 (2024-06-20). ChartQAPro's 'Claude Sonnet 3.5 scores 90.5% on ChartQA' is cited from reports, not an organizer re-run. Strict: no independent/organizer-verified single-model >=90 found; Qwen3-VL report's independent runs of frontier models were below 90 (Claude Opus 4.1 86.2, Gemini 2.5 Pro ~83, GPT-5 ~60) - shows strong prompt/format sensitivity but no rerun of Claude 3.5 Sonnet itself, so the self-report is not treated as refuted. Labs stopped reporting after 2025-06 (last: Mistral Small 3.2, 2025-06-20).

canonical_name: DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images (Mathew, Karatzas, Jawahar; WACV 2021) - Single Document VQA, RRC Task 1
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.08899 (DocVQA 2020 challenge report: 'The challenge ran between March and May 2020'); paper https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.00398 (v1 2020-07-01); docvqa.org news '[May 2020] DocVQA 2020 Challenge ends and results are published'
metric: ANLS (Average Normalized Levenshtein Similarity, 0-1, usually reported x100) on the test split via the RRC evaluation server
score_at_release_system: BERT-large (SQuAD) fine-tuned on DocVQA, test ANLS 0.665 (paper baseline); 2020 challenge winner PingAn-OneConnect-Gammalab-DQA 0.85 (May 2020)
n_items: 5,188 test questions on 1,287 document images (train 39,463 / val 5,349; ~50K questions, 12K images)
lineage: Family maintained by CVC-UAB/IIIT-H: DocVQA (2020) -> DocCVQA, InfographicVQA (2021-04), MP-DocVQA (2022), DocVQA2026 / ICDAR 2026 competition on multimodal reasoning over documents in 8 domains (site live 2025-11-28; does not cite saturation).
best_by_cutoff: Self-reported: 97.1 - Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct (DocVQA test, Qwen3-VL tech report arXiv 2511.21631, model release 2025-09); Seed1.5-VL 96.9 scored via the official server (arXiv 2505.07062, 2025-05); public RRC leaderboard top: qwen2-vl 0.9670 (2024-07-11)
notes: Human performance: 'We collect answers for all questions in test split, with help of a few volunteers from our institution' -> ANLS 0.981 / acc 94.36% on the same test split; RRC leaderboard shows 'Human Performance' 0.9811 (2020-06-13) -> criterion A (>=85%). No submission on the official RRC Task-1 leaderboard reaches 0.9811 (top-15 checked via docvqa/RRC page, max 0.9670); best self-reports 96.4-97.1 (Qwen2/2.5/3-VL) - alive. Sensitivity: under criterion B (90 ANLS) the event would be ~2022-10 (RRC entry BAIDU-DI 0.9016, 2022-10-08; SMoLA-PaLI-X 0.9084 2023-11; Gemini Ultra self-report 90.9 2023-12). DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 'DocVQA (LLM-Judge)' 95.6 (2026-09-10) is a base-model, LLM-judged variant, not ANLS.

canonical_name: ERQA (Embodied Reasoning Question Answering), Google DeepMind - introduced with Gemini Robotics / Gemini Robotics-ER
release_source: https://github.com/embodiedreasoning/ERQA (dataset commit 2025-03-08, README links to Gemini Robotics release blog/tech report 2025-03-12); tech report https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.20020 (v1 2025-03-25)
metric: accuracy (%) on multiple-choice questions (single letter A-D), 400 examples
score_at_release_system: Gemini 2.0 Pro Experimental with chain-of-thought (48.3 without CoT; GPT-4o 50.5 CoT) - Gemini Robotics tech report
n_items: 400 (spatial 84, action 72, trajectory 66, state estimation 55, task 38, multi-view 37, pointing 34)
lineage: Released with Gemini Robotics-ER (2025-03); used as headline embodied-reasoning eval for Gemini Robotics-ER 1.5/1.6/2. Images partly from OXE, UMI, MECCANO, HoloAssist, EGTEA Gaze+. No successor version found.
best_by_cutoff: 77.8 - Qwen3.8-Max (Qwen blog qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen3.8, 2026-08-03, per input lab report; blog not machine-readable); Google DeepMind product page lists Gemini Robotics-ER 2 at 78.5 (undated, fetched 2026-10) and Gemini 3.6 Flash 73.0
notes: No human baseline in the tech report -> criterion B (90). Trajectory: GPT-5 65.7 (2025-08-07), Qwen3.5 67.5 (2026-02), Gemini 3 Pro 70.5 (Qwen-run), Muse Spark 64.7 (2026-04), Qwen3.7-Plus 69.8 (2026-06), Qwen3.8-Max 77.8 (2026-08); far from 90 by cutoff. Question labels were manually created by the authors ('We manually labeled all questions').

canonical_name: EgoSchema: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Very Long-form Video Language Understanding (Mangalam, Akshulakov, Malik; NeurIPS 2023 D&B)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.09126 (v1 2023-08-17); repo https://github.com/egoschema/EgoSchema (README/instructions commits 2023-08-17, subset answers released 2023-08-31)
metric: accuracy (%) on 5-way multiple-choice questions over 3-minute egocentric clips, full set (answers hidden; scored via Kaggle 'egoschema-public' / validation server)
score_at_release_system: InternVideo (478M, 90 frames) - best model in the paper (random 20%)
n_items: 5,031 questions in the full evaluation set (README; paper says 5,063 instances); answers public for a 500-question subset only
lineage: Built on Ego4D videos/narrations; questions LLM-generated then filtered and human-curated in two rounds. Related successors in long-video QA: Video-MME, MLVU, LVBench (2024). No official successor version.
best_by_cutoff: 78.5 - Kimi-VL-A3B (EgoSchema full, Moonshot tech report arXiv 2504.07491, 2025-04-10); frontier-lab self-reports: Grok 3 Beta 74.5 (2025-02-19), GPT-4o 72.2 (2024-05-13)
notes: Human accuracy measured by annotators on a sample (~9 h of video): 76.2% unconstrained (67-68% under 1-3 min limits) -> < 85 -> criterion B (90). Full-set scores are only obtainable through the Kaggle submission channel (README: 'the entire correct answer file will not be made public'); the promised public ranking page is still 'Coming Soon'. No result near 90 found (best ~78.5). Abandonment check: last reports by the 9 labs are Kimi-VL (2025-04-10, 78.5) and Meta PerceptionLM (arXiv 2504.13180, 2025-04-17, PLM-8B 68.8); not in Gemini 2.5 report (2025-06), Qwen3-Omni (2025-09) or Qwen3-VL (2025-11) -> >17 months without lab reports by cutoff. But the official Kaggle leaderboard (egoschema-public) could not be read (JS page), so '>=12 months without leaderboard activity' is unverified and academic papers continue to submit full-set results; coded alive (would be 'abandoned, 2025-04' if the Kaggle board is inactive). Input lab list ends 2025-02-19 (Grok 3) but misses Kimi-VL/PLM.

canonical_name: InfographicVQA (Mathew, Bagal, Tito, Karatzas, Valveny, Jawahar; WACV 2022) - Task 3 of the DocVQA 2021 challenge
release_source: https://www.docvqa.org/challenges/2021 ('December 2020: Released train split for the new infographics VQA'; val/test splits released 2021-01-10 [page says 'January 10, 2020', evidently 2021]); paper https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.12756 (v1 2021-04-26)
metric: ANLS (0-1, reported x100) on the test split via the RRC evaluation server
score_at_release_system: LayoutLM-based baseline (test ANLS 0.272; paper); 2021 challenge winner TILT 0.612 (2021-04-11)
n_items: 3,288 test questions on 579 infographics (train 23,946 / val 2,801; 30,035 total)
lineage: Sibling of DocVQA (2020-03) in the CVC-UAB/IIIT-H DocVQA family; later family member DocVQA2026 (ICDAR 2026 competition). No InfographicVQA v2.
best_by_cutoff: 92.6 - Kimi K2.5 thinking (InfoVQA val, github.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-K2.5 README, 2026-01); on test: Seed1.5-VL thinking 91.2 (scored by uploading to the official leaderboard; arXiv 2505.07062, 2025-05-11), Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Thinking 89.5 (arXiv 2511.21631)
notes: Human performance: 'all questions in the test split ... answered with the help of two volunteers' -> ANLS 0.980 / acc 95.70 on the same test split -> criterion A (>=85%); threshold 98.0 ANLS not approached (best self-reports 84-93). Note Kimi K2.5 reports InfoVQA on val (split=dev; its tech report table labels it test - inconsistent). Sensitivity: under criterion B (90 ANLS) the first crossing found is Seed1.5-VL thinking 91.2 on test via the official leaderboard (Seed1.5-VL report 2025-05-11: 'We collect scores by uploading prediction to the official leaderboard'); earlier Gemini Ultra 80.3 (2023-12), Gemini 1.5 Pro 72.7/81.0, Qwen2-VL-72B 84.5, InternVL2.5-78B 84.1, Qwen2.5-VL-72B 87.3 were below 90; Kimi K2.5 92.6 (val, 2026-01). RRC Task-3 page shows only the frozen 2021 competition ranking (top TILT 0.612).

canonical_name: LVBench: An Extreme Long Video Understanding Benchmark (Wang et al., Tsinghua/Zhipu AI, 2024)
release_source: https://github.com/zai-org/LVBench (README news '2024.06.11 We released LVBench'; repo init 2024-06-13); https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.08035 (v1 2024-06-12)
metric: accuracy (%) on 4-option multiple-choice questions over long videos (overall)
lineage: Long-video QA family with EgoSchema (2023-08), MLVU (2024-06), Video-MME (2024-05), LongVideoBench (2024-07). Same group's paper updated to v3 (2025-08) with newer models; no successor version.
best_by_cutoff: 87.8 - Gemini 3.8 Flash, agentic setting (model card deepmind.google/models/model-cards/gemini-3-8-flash, 2026-09; same row shows 87.1 'static' for another column); Gemini 3.7 Flash 85.4 (2026-08-13); Qwen3.8-Max 85.6 with memory (2026-08-03). Official leaderboard (lvbench.github.io, last update 2025-06-29) top: Deep Video Discovery (Microsoft agent) 74.2.
notes: Paper reports 'humans achieve a very high accuracy of 94.4% on average' (per-category 87.4-98.4, Table 3) but gives no protocol (number of annotators, sample, viewing conditions) -> A's 'described protocol' condition not met -> criterion B (90); under A (94.4) status is the same. No result >= 90 by cutoff: frontier trajectory Gemini 2.5 Pro 78.7 (audio+visual, 2025-06-17; LVBench v3 table lists 67.4 under its own setting), Kimi K2.5 75.9 (2026-01), Gemini 3.8 Flash 87.8 agentic (2026-09). Agentic/memory scaffolds are accepted on the official leaderboard (e.g., Deep Video Discovery), so they would count in main mode, but none reach 90. Official HF Spaces leaderboard not checked (site leaderboard used).

canonical_name: LingoQA: Visual Question Answering for Autonomous Driving (Marcu et al., Wayve; ECCV 2024) - evaluation benchmark scored with Lingo-Judge
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.14115 (v1 2023-12-21); repo https://github.com/wayveai/LingoQA (README 2023-12-21; benchmark code and datasets released 2024-03-19/26)
metric: Lingo-Judge accuracy (%): share of answers classified as correct by the learned text classifier wayveai/Lingo-Judge against reference answers
score_at_release_system: LingoQA baseline model, 5 frames (GPT-4V 59.6) - paper Table 5
n_items: 500 evaluation questions (1,000 reference QA pairs, 2 answers per question) on 100 driving scenarios
lineage: Wayve's driving VQA dataset (Scenery 267.8k + Action 152.5k training QA) with the Lingo-Judge metric; related driving-VLM benchmarks DriveLM, NuScenes-QA. No successor version found.
best_by_cutoff: 84.8 - Qwen3.8-Max (Qwen blog qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen3.8, 2026-08-03, per input lab report; blog not machine-readable); Qwen3.7-Plus 83.4 (2026-06-01); Qwen3.5-397B 81.6 (HF card 2026-02-16, where Claude 4.5 Opus scored 78.8 in Qwen's comparison)
notes: Human row 'Human (5 frames) 96.6%' Lingo-Judge accuracy on the evaluation set (abstract: 'GPT-4V responding truthfully to 59.6% of the questions compared to 96.6% for humans'); protocol details (number of people) only partly available to me -> treated as average human -> criterion A (96.6). Under B (90) status would be identical (best 84.8). Only Qwen reports LingoQA among the 9 labs (3 releases, 2026-02 to 2026-08). Lingo-Judge is a fine-tuned text classifier (0.95 Spearman with human ratings), hence class LLM-judge.

canonical_name: MATH-Vision (MATH-V): Measuring Multimodal Mathematical Reasoning with MATH-Vision Dataset (Wang et al., CUHK MMLab; NeurIPS 2024 D&B) - full test set
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14804 (v1 2024-02-22); repo https://github.com/mathllm/MATH-V (news '[2024-02-22] ... GPT-4V only scores 23.98%')
metric: accuracy (%) on the full 3,040-problem test set (multiple-choice and free-form numeric answers; 'ALL' column of the official leaderboard)
